items.headline: Alberta votes to stay in Canada
items.summary: Alberta voters rejected a move toward independence in a nonbinding referendum, according to early results. The outcome boosts Prime Minister Mark Carney's push for national unity.

items.headline: Trump escalates feud with Zelenskyy
items.summary: President Trump again criticized Ukraine's president as Russia kept up deadly strikes, including fresh attacks on the power grid. Zelenskyy said Ukraine got no early warning from partners and objected to U.S. moves that benefit Moscow.

items.headline: Trump open to summit with Putin and Xi
items.summary: TIME reports Trump is open to a "denuclearization" summit with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. Putin had proposed a three-way meeting tied to ending the Ukraine war.

items.headline: France imposes curfews after riots
items.summary: French authorities imposed curfews in parts of Paris and other cities after weekend rioting and looting. The interior minister acknowledged police lost control in some places.

items.headline: DOJ charges 28 in California voting probe
items.summary: The Justice Department charged 28 people in California with voting crimes. It also sought an emergency court order to stop the state from processing ballots from people it calls likely noncitizens.

items.headline: Australian lawmaker hit by car in deliberate attack
items.summary: Independent federal lawmaker Helen Haines was critically injured when a vehicle struck her outside her office in Victoria. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said it was no accident, and the driver was arrested.

items.headline: Midterm ad spending tops $10 billion
items.summary: Political ad spending in the 2026 midterms has passed $10 billion, driven by super PACs and billionaire donors. Major Senate races are drawing hundreds of millions of dollars.

items.headline: TikTok ignored child-safety warnings, records show
items.summary: Court records show TikTok staff raised internal alarms about child safety. Executives failed to act on the warnings, according to the records.

items.headline: Japan launches mission to Mars moon
items.summary: Japan launched a spacecraft on a five-year mission to land on the Martian moon Phobos and bring back soil samples. The mission combines the work of five space agencies.

items.headline: El Niño brings tropical sea life to California
items.summary: A powerful El Niño is pushing unusually warm water up the California coast. Tropical sea creatures rarely seen there are arriving with it.

digest.overview:
President Trump said it may be time for someone else to negotiate on Ukraine's behalf, deepening his rift with Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The Justice Department charged 28 people in California with voting crimes and asked a court to halt processing of ballots from people it calls likely noncitizens. A federal judge sharply criticized the administration's plan to press ahead with overhauling a historic Washington golf course. The Supreme Court declined to review Trump's firing of a labor board member. Homeland Security granted a temporary deportation reprieve to more than 100,000 Ukrainians and Sudanese. Midterm ad spending has passed $10 billion two weeks before Election Day.

Abroad, Alberta voted decisively to stay in Canada, with about 76% backing unity in early returns. A Russian strike on Kyiv left more than half a million households without power, while Ukraine said it launched over 1,000 drones at Russia. TIME reported Trump is open to a summit with Putin and Xi, though the Kremlin said nothing is arranged. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Israel, Iran said it downed a U.S. drone over the Strait of Hormuz, and the World Food Programme cut Gaza aid to 1.1 million people from 1.6 million. France extended curfews to Nice, Lyon and parts of Gironde after riots. Japan launched its MMX probe to collect samples from Mars' moon Phobos. North Korea threatened more deployments and propaganda broadcasts along the border as Seoul vowed a firm response. Australian lawmaker Helen Haines was critically injured in what officials called a deliberate car attack.

home.overview:
The Rays are going to the World Series after a 7–3 Game 6 win over Cleveland, with Junior Caminero and Yandy Díaz each hitting two-run homers and Freddy Peralta named ALCS MVP; Tampa Bay and Milwaukee guarantee a first-time champion when Game 1 opens Friday at the Brewers. On Monday night the 49ers beat the Commanders 23–17 to reach 6–0, but Washington lost Terry McLaurin to a knee injury, and the Eagles expect Jalen Hurts to miss the rest of the season with blood clots. The NBA season tips off tonight with Celtics–Pistons, LeBron James' 76ers debut at the Knicks, and Thunder–Spurs, a day after the Lakers waived Dalton Knecht.

Tottenham finally won in the Premier League, beating Coventry 3–1 behind goals from James Maddison, Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies, while Getafe and Rayo Vallecano drew 1–1. The Champions League returns tonight with PSG hosting Barcelona, and Bayern welcome Arsenal on Wednesday ahead of Sunday's Clásico at Barcelona. The FA Cup first-round draw sent Leicester to sixth-tier Oxford City, FC Seoul can clinch the K League 1 title on Saturday, and Columbus play for the U.S. Open Cup on Wednesday. In the KBO, Kia can sweep LG with a win in Tuesday's Game 3 at Jamsil.
